- Validate input: ensure n is a positive integer; handle n == 1 as 1; optionally raise for n <= 0.
- Iterate k from 1 to n, maintain an accumulating factorial current_fact (starting at 1) and multiply it into a running product result at each step; update current_fact *= k each iteration.
- Return result; use Python’s big integers (no special handling) and avoid recomputing factorials from scratch for efficiency.
